task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:

turns.thought:
Good news — I found the likely cause. I pulled up your account, John (customer C1001), and your line **555-123-2002** (line L1002, Premium Plan).

Here's what I found and did:

**1. Roaming was not enabled — now fixed.**
Because you're in France (outside our home network), your line needs international roaming enabled to use mobile data at all. It was turned **off** on your line, which explains why data stopped working entirely at times. I have now **enabled roaming on your line at no cost**. I verified the change took effect.

**2. Data usage is fine — no overage.**
You've used **8.7 GB of your 15 GB** plan allowance for this billing cycle (cycle ends 2025-02-28), so you have not hit your data limit.

**3. Your line is in good standing.**
Line status is Active, contract runs through 2026-12-31, and no suspension applies to this line.

**What I need you to do on your phone now:**
- Go to **Settings → Connections/Cellular → Mobile Networks** and make sure **Data Roaming** is switched **ON** (this is the phone-side toggle that works together with what I enabled).
- Then **restart (reboot) your device** so it can re-register on a French partner network.
- Test your mobile data afterward and let me know if it's working and how the speed is.

If it's still slow after that, tell me and we'll check further (e.g., Data Saver mode, VPN, or your network mode preference).

One other note: your current bill **B1002** for $150.00 was due 2025-02-19 and still shows an outstanding balance. Would you like to take care of that now as well?
turns.execution_output: User: Well, thank you for finding that. I'll try to do what you said... Let me see if I can turn on that roaming thing on my phone.

turns.thought:
Good news: Data Roaming ON is the big one, and you've done it. And let's absolutely focus on the internet first — we'll leave the bill for later.

**First, about restarting your phone — your photos are safe.** A restart simply powers the phone off and back on; it refreshes the system's running services and network connections. It does not delete photos, contacts, messages, or apps. Your grandchildren's pictures will be there when it comes back on. (Turning the phone back on is just the normal power button — nothing gets erased.)

Now, three things on your screen that explain the "poor" experience:

**1. The "2G" — this is the main cause of the slowness.**
2G is a very old, very slow network technology. It's enough for a basic call, but it can barely load anything else and won't carry picture messages. We want your phone to prefer 4G or 5G instead.

Please do this on your phone:
- **Settings → Connections (or Network & Internet) → Mobile Networks → Network Mode / Preferred Network Mode**
- Select **5G/4G preferred** (it may be labeled "4G/3G/2G auto" or "LTE" — choose the option that includes 5G or 4G/LTE)
- Then select the **3G or 4G/5G** option if it asks you to pick one specifically

**2. The little lock icon — VPN is connected.**
A VPN routes all your internet traffic through an extra server, which can make things much slower, and it can also block picture messaging. Since you're abroad, let's turn it off for now:
- **Settings → Network & Internet → VPN** (or open the VPN app you use)
- Tap the connected VPN and choose **Disconnect**

If the VPN is something your work or a specific app requires, just disconnect it temporarily while we get the speed fixed — you can reconnect later.

**3. After both of the above, restart your phone** so the phone re-registers on a faster French network.

So, in order: **switch the network mode off 2G → disconnect the VPN → restart the phone.**

Once it's back on, please check the top of your screen again and tell me:
- Does it now show **4G, LTE, or 5G** instead of 2G?
- Is the **lock/VPN icon** gone?
- Do web pages and apps load better?

If it still shows 2G after changing the setting, that may mean the only network available right where you are is 2G — tell me and we'll look at it together.
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh my, that's a lot of steps all at once. I'm afraid I can only do one thing at a time — I get confused easily with all these menus. Could you please tell me just the first thing to do, one step at a time? 

I'm glad to hear my photos will be safe, though. That's a relief. So... what's the very first thing you'd like me to do?

turns.thought:
Of course — one step at a time. Let's do the network mode first, since that's what's making things slow.

**Step 1 — Switch off "2G" (just this one thing):**

1. Open **Settings** (the gear icon).
2. Tap **Connections** (on some phones it's called **Network & Internet** or **Mobile Networks**).
3. Tap **Mobile Networks**.
4. Tap **Network Mode** (it may be called **Preferred Network Mode** or **Preferred Network Type**).
5. Choose the option that mentions **5G** — for example **"5G/LTE/3G/2G auto"** or **"5G/4G preferred"**.

That's it — just that one menu and one tap. Take your time.

**Tell me when you've done it** (or if you can't find that menu, just tell me what you see on the screen and I'll help you from there). Once that's done, I'll give you exactly one next step. No rush at all.

Wonderful — "Excellent" with **5G** is a huge improvement over 2G. That was the main fix, and you did it.

**Step 2 — Turn off the VPN (just this one thing):**

1. Open **Settings** (the gear icon).
2. Tap **Network & Internet** (on some phones: **Connections** → **More connection settings**).
3. Tap **VPN**.
4. You should see the VPN you're connected to. Tap the **gear icon or settings icon** next to it (on some phones just tap its name).
5. Tap **Disconnect** (or **Forget VPN** / **Turn off**).

The little 🔒 lock icon at the top should disappear once it's done.

Take your time — and tell me whether the lock icon is gone. If you'd rather not disconnect it (for example, if it's for your work), just say so and we'll leave it in place.

Yes — restarting is the right next step, and it's the last one. And I completely understand the nervousness, so let me say it once more clearly:

**A restart will not delete anything.** It's the same as when your phone battery runs out and you turn it back on — no photos, no contacts, no messages, no apps are touched. Your grandchildren's pictures stay exactly where they are.

**Step 3 — Restart your phone:**

1. Press and **hold the power button** (the button you normally use to wake or lock the screen).
2. When a menu appears on the screen, tap **Restart** (on some phones it says **Reboot**).
   - If you don't see a "Restart" option, tap **Power off** instead — wait about 30 seconds for the screen to go fully dark — then press and hold the power button again to turn it back on.
3. Wait for the phone to boot back up (this can take a minute or so).

After it comes back on:
- Unlock your phone.
- Check the top of the screen — you should still see the signal bars and **5G**.
- Try opening a webpage or an app that needs the internet to see if it works and feels faster.

Take all the time you need. When it's back up, just tell me: **does it still show 5G, and is the internet working?** Then we'll know we're done. (If it isn't working, we'll keep going — nothing is lost either way.)

Yes, please do — that's the final check. Go ahead and try it now.

**Step 4 — Test the internet (just this one thing):**

1. Open your web browser (Chrome, Safari, or whatever you usually use).
2. Try loading any webpage you like.
3. Optionally, try one app that needs internet — perhaps the photo app syncing, your email, or a map.

Take your time, and then tell me:
- Does the page load?
- Does it feel reasonably quick, or still slow?

If it loads well, then we're all done — the fix was enabling roaming together with switching off the "2G" setting, and your line is in great shape: **Active**, contract through 2026-12-31, and you've used **8.7 GB of your 15 GB** allowance with no data limit issue.

If it still doesn't load, tell me exactly what you see (any error message, or just a blank/loading screen) and we'll keep working on it step by step. And if a picture message is giving you trouble too, let me know — that's a separate thing we can look at after this.

Wonderful — 275 Mbps is excellent. Everything looks fixed: roaming is enabled, you're on 5G with an excellent signal, the VPN is off, and your data usage (8.7 GB of 15 GB) is well within your plan. And no plan change is needed — I won't touch that.

Now let me check that bill for you.
